newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rail unions call to back trucker protests.
newsitem.headline: French rail unions call to back trucker protests.

text.p: Trade unions at France's SNCF state railways issued a joint statement on Monday backing widening protests by truck drivers, saying rail workers should back the protests "in the way they will judge necessary."
The communique was jointly signed by the Communist-led CGT, the CFDT, which is the country's largest labout union, as well as Force Ouvriere the CFTC and the FMC.

In an attached statement signed only by itself, the CGT union said it wanted "all union groupings involved in this conflict to make November 27 a day of mobilisation and demonstration and a show of unity at the road blockades."

The truckers strike, sparked by demands for higher wages, shorter hours and retirement at age 55 rather than 60, went into its eighth day on Monday after the breakdown of marathon talks through Sunday night between truckers and employers.
SNCF railworkers spearheaded a crippling public sector strike for more than three weeks last November and December.
Neither the statement signed by the five rail unions nor the statement signed by the CGT alone spoke of strikes.

"This (truckers') conflict, after that of the railworkers, once again puts the spotlight on the necessity of defining a real transport policy, allowing for complementarity between the modes of transport and an upgrading of social conditions across the sector," the joint statement said.
"The CGT, CFDT, FO, CFTC and FMC union federations call on railworkers to back -- in the way they will judge necessary -- the actions of road transport workers," it said.
"We warn the government and SNCF management against any attempt to pit transport employees against one another," said the communique.

The separate CGT statement, clearly designed at widening the conflict, called on local, regional and national level union organisations to mobilise on November 27 in defence of better wages, work conditions and employment.
"Employer intransigence towards the truck drivers shows it is vital to widen labour movement pressure to oblige employers to respond other than by distrust and stubbornness," it added.
